description: Poorly dated Late Iron Age enclosure, at the centre of the enclosure was a large sarsen stone surrounded by many burnt patches and a large pit containing charcoal, pottery, and a horse jaw. A temporary animal enclosure has been proposed, but the RSRB prefers a ritual interpretation and has marked the site as a 'shrine'.
bibliography: Chambers. “An Iron Age Enclosure at Hailey Wood, Lewknor.” Oxoniensia 38 (1973).
Martyn, Blick, Brindle, and et al. “Hailey Wood, Lewknor (Oxfordshire).” The Rural Settlement of Roman Britain: an online resource, 2015. https://doi.org/10.5284/1030449.
